intro.quote: The signaling protocol model uses downstream-on-demand label distribution. A request to bind labels to a specific LSP tunnel is initiated by an ingress node through the RSVP Path message. For this purpose, the RSVP Path message is augmented with a LABEL_REQUEST object. Labels are allocated downstream and distributed (propagated upstream) by means of the RSVP Resv message. For this purpose, the RSVP Resv message is extended with a special LABEL object.

steps.explain: The ingress node creates a Path message for an LSP tunnel and includes LABEL_REQUEST to request a label binding and identify the carried network-layer protocol.

cite.quote: To create an LSP tunnel, the first MPLS node on the path -- that is, the sender node with respect to the path -- creates an RSVP Path message with a session type of LSP_TUNNEL_IPv4 or LSP_TUNNEL_IPv6 and inserts a LABEL_REQUEST object into the Path message.

steps.explain: The destination returns a Resv message with a LABEL object associated with the applicable filter.

cite.quote: The destination node of a label-switched path responds to a LABEL_REQUEST by including a LABEL object in its response RSVP Resv message. The LABEL object is inserted in the filter spec list immediately following the filter spec to which it pertains.

intro.quote: In general, it is highly desirable not to disrupt traffic, or adversely impact network operations while TE tunnel rerouting is in progress. This adaptive and smooth rerouting requirement necessitates establishing a new LSP tunnel and transferring traffic from the old LSP tunnel onto it before tearing down the old LSP tunnel. This concept is called "make-before-break."

steps.explain: The ingress keeps the original session but creates a new sender template and explicit route, then signals the replacement path while continuing to refresh the old path.

cite.quote: To effect a reroute, the ingress node picks a new LSP ID and forms a new SENDER_TEMPLATE. The ingress node then creates a new ERO to define the new path. Thereafter the node sends a new Path Message using the original SESSION object and the new SENDER_TEMPLATE and ERO. It continues to use the old LSP and refresh the old Path message.

steps.explain: The reservation for the new path returns to the ingress, enabling traffic to move to the replacement.

cite.quote: Once the ingress node receives a Resv message for the new LSP, it can transition traffic to it and tear down the old LSP.

steps.explain: After the new reservation arrives, the ingress may use the new route and should remove the old route with a PathTear message.

cite.quote: When the ingress node receives the Resv Message(s), it may begin using the new route. It SHOULD send a PathTear message for the old route.

intro.quote: Type 1 is a Label Request without label range.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.explain: This reserved area is sent as zero and ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: Reserved This field is reserved. It MUST be set to zero on transmission and MUST be ignored on receipt.

fields.name: L3PID
fields.explain: Identifies the layer-three protocol carried on the path using standard Ethertype values.

cite.quote: L3PID an identifier of the layer 3 protocol using this path. Standard Ethertype values are used.

intro.quote: The contents of an IPv4 prefix subobject are a 4-octet IPv4 address, a 1-octet prefix length, and a 1-octet pad.

fields.name: L
fields.explain: Indicates whether the subobject represents a loose or strict hop in the explicit route.

cite.quote: The L bit is an attribute of the subobject. The L bit is set if the subobject represents a loose hop in the explicit route. If the bit is not set, the subobject represents a strict hop in the explicit route.

fields.name: Type
fields.explain: Identifies the subobject as an IPv4 address.

fields.name: Length
fields.explain: Gives the total subobject length in bytes.

cite.quote: Length The Length contains the total length of the subobject in bytes, including the Type and Length fields. The Length is always 8.

fields.name: IPv4 address
fields.explain: Holds the IPv4 address treated as a prefix, with bits outside the prefix ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: IPv4 address An IPv4 address. This address is treated as a prefix based on the prefix length value below. Bits beyond the prefix are ignored on receipt and SHOULD be set to zero on transmission.

fields.name: Prefix Length
fields.explain: Gives the IPv4 prefix length in bits.

cite.quote: Prefix length Length in bits of the IPv4 prefix

fields.name: Padding
fields.explain: Is sent as zero and ignored on receipt.

cite.quote: Padding Zero on transmission. Ignored on receipt.
